name: Powdered Azurite
summary: In Hillsbrad Foothills, Powdered Azurite is taken from the Azurelode Mine. Thun'grim Firegaze needs it to forge brutal armor for rising Horde warriors.

sections.title: A Rare Mineral Compound
sections.body: Powdered Azurite comes from the mineral veins beneath Hillsbrad Foothills. Human workers dig the blue stone from Azurelode Mine, then grind and pack it for trade and metalworking. A skilled smith mixes the dust with dense metals to make armor more durable and resilient.

sections.title: Forging Brutal Armor
sections.body: Horde blacksmiths prize Powdered Azurite for its strength in metalworking, though it comes from human-held tunnels across the Great Sea. Thun'grim Firegaze, an aging orc armorer in the Barrens, asks for small amounts alongside refined iron and fiery reagents. Mixed into the smelt, the powder helps him hammer out the heavy plating of his Brutal Armor.

faq.q: What is Powdered Azurite used for?
faq.answer: Thun'grim Firegaze uses Powdered Azurite with iron ingots and volatile reagents to forge pieces of Brutal Armor for Horde champions.

faq.q: Where can Powdered Azurite be found?
faq.answer: Human miners gather Powdered Azurite in Azurelode Mine, along the southern coast of the Hillsbrad Foothills in the Eastern Kingdoms.

faq.q: Why does an armorer in the Barrens require reagents from Hillsbrad?
faq.answer: Thun'grim Firegaze seeks fine materials for armor worthy of legendary warriors. Iron is easy to find, but the tempering qualities of Azurelode mineral make it worth sending his champions across the sea to obtain.

angles.text: As a warrior, gathering Powdered Azurite tests your endurance abroad and brings Thun'grim Firegaze the reagents he needs to forge your armor of savage strength.
As a member of the Horde, claiming this refined dust means striking deep into the Eastern Kingdoms and taking resources from Alliance hands in Hillsbrad Foothills.
